title: Senior Embedded Software Developer
location: Copenhagen Municipality, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
description: Oticon Medical is seeking a Senior Embedded Software Developer to join our team in developing next-generation bone conduction hearing aids. The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in embedded systems, Bluetooth Low Energy (LE) technology, and software development in a regulated environment. Responsibilities You will join a small and highly skilled team, working towards a new generation of bone conduction hearing aids independently from the technology previously used. You will play a key role in implementing and maturing our embedded software platform in close collaboration with the rest of the cross-functional development team. Your main responsibilities will be: Develop and maintain embedded software for a system-on-chip (SoC) platform with an ARM core Implement, integrate and mature Bluetooth Low Energy audio and data functionality Translate architectural designs into robust, maintainable, and efficient software solutions Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, including DSP engineers, PC software developers, and electronics designers Take technical ownership of selected software modules and drive them from implementation through verification Implement robust testing and verification processes to ensure the software meets all functional, quality, and regulatory requirements. Working according to our Oticon Medical development cycle, which complies with regulatory requirements, to implement, optimize, verify, and document solutions. Technical background The candidate should hold a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related field. Besides, we expect that you can tick off most of the following: Solid experience in embedded software development using C/C++ Experience with Bluetooth Low Energy for audio and data. Familiarity with ARM-based SoCs and real-time operating systems (RTOS) Knowledge of audio streaming protocols and low-latency communication Experience with medical device software development and regulatory compliance Ability to produce high-quality, maintainable code Knowledge of good software practices, such as software design, unit testing and continuous integration Experience debugging complex embedded systems across software and hardware boundaries As a professional, you possess keen social intelligence and are fluent in English (Danish is a plus). You are committed to finding solutions to hard problems and skilled in discussing unknowns and documenting the outcome. You are creative in finding solutions to challenges and experienced at handling issues and setbacks. You enjoy teamwork and thrive in an environment where technical discussions and collaborative problem solving are part of everyday work. Work environment The Oticon Medical BAHS R&D organization consists of 60 people, split between the headquarters in Gothenburg, Sweden; Smørum, Denmark; and Sophia Antipolis, France. Due to the size of our organization, we do not plan to develop everything in-house but rather utilize subcontractors or strategic partners for parts of the development. Our strategy is to be small and agile, and to accomplish this task we need to make unconventional choices and be pragmatic. This position is open for the office in Smørum, Denmark, where we are currently 21 people located. Position is mainly on site. Come join us! You can look forward to a role filled with opportunities to learn and shape the future of bone-anchored hearing. We are developing products that truly make a difference for end users in a field ripe with potential for innovation. How To Apply This is a full-time position based at our headquarters in Smørum, Greater Copenhagen. We encourage you to submit your CV and a brief motivation letter through our online application portal no later than 18 October 2026 . Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. If you have any questions about the position, please feel free to contact Simon Krogholt, Director, Sound Processor Systems, at skch@oticonmedical.com. We expect to conduct interviews in week 43. At Oticon Medical we value diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I) and we are committed to creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of ethnic background, personality, age, gender, and education. Diversity is part of our cultural DNA. Women in STEM areas are particularly encouraged to apply, as Oticon Medical supports United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5 on gender equality.
